description: Detection/non-detection of boreal chorus frog, boreal toad, western tiger salamander, columbia spotted frog at 145 wetland sites in 36 catchments, Bridger-Teton National Forest, Wyoming, 2014-2019 (Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project), 1-8 surveys per site-year, with site area, isolation metrics, coordinates, survey date, observer count and surveyor type.
reference: Addis, B. (2026). Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project occupancy data and analyses [Data set]. figshare.
notes: One of two tables from the deposit (split by national forest because the species pools differ). No air temperature in this forest's files.

description: Detection/non-detection of boreal chorus frog, boreal toad, western tiger salamander, northern leopard frog, wood frog at 188 wetland sites in 35 catchments, Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, Wyoming/Colorado, 2012-2019 (Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project), 1-8 surveys per site-year, with site area, isolation metrics, coordinates, survey date, observer count and surveyor type.
reference: Addis, B. (2026). Rocky Mountain Amphibian Project occupancy data and analyses [Data set]. figshare.
notes: One of two tables from the deposit (split by national forest because the species pools differ). Squared air temperature from the wood frog file shipped as obs_air_temp_f_sq.

description: Camera-trap distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: 91 cameras at six 1 km sites, night-time 1 s snapshot detections in twelve 1 m radial-distance bins per camera, with seconds deployed as effort and hares per bin. 3,706 detections. First camera-trap distance-sampling table; one of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): camera-trap distance sampling, occasion = 1 m radial bin, snapshotInterval 1 s, effort in seconds. Sibling tables: _vis_ds, _therm_ds.

description: Night-time thermal-imaging point-transect distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: 114 visits to 71 vantage points at six 1 km sites, hare groups in eight radial-distance bins (50 m to 350 m, then 350-750 m) per visit, with hares per bin. 206 detections. One of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = radial-distance bin (point transect). Visits recovered from row order (matches the paper's replicate counts). Processor-binned distances. Sibling tables: _vis_ds, _cam_ds.

description: Daylight line-transect distance sampling of mountain hares (Lepus timidus) at six 1 km sites on Holme Moss, Peak District, winter 2017-18: hare groups in five perpendicular-distance bins (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20-100, 100-400 m) per site walk, with walk length and hares per bin. 41 detections. One of three sibling tables comparing survey methods.
reference: Bedson, C. P. E., Thomas, L., Wheeler, P. M., Reid, N., Harris, W. E., Lloyd, H., Mallon, D., & Preziosi, R. (2021). Estimating density of mountain hares using distance sampling: a comparison of daylight visual surveys, night-time thermal imaging and camera traps. Wildlife Biology, 2021(3), wlb.00802.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = distance bin. Continuous distances binned by the processor to the paper's breaks plus a 100-400 m bin. Six walks only. Sibling tables: _therm_ds, _cam_ds.

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of Asiatic black bear at 67 camera sites in two Himachal Pradesh wildlife sanctuaries (Rupi Bhaba 2019, Daranghati 2018), up to 49 camera-days each; 58 detections in 2,326 camera-days; no coordinates.
reference: Bhattacharya, A., Chatterjee, N., Angrish, K., Meena, D., Sinha, B. C. & Habib, B. (2022). Population estimation of Asiatic black bear in the Himalayan Region of India using camera traps. Ursus 33(e8), 1-10.
notes: Two protected areas sampled in different years, shipped as one table with cluster_id = area. Camera-relative day occasions, no dates. Paper paywalled; abstract used.

description: Daily detection/non-detection of the Alpine mountain hare at 46 camera-trap stations (1,227-2,740 m) in the Mont-Blanc massif, France, September 2017 to June 2022, binned into 20 meteorological seasons, with surveyed camera-days from setup dates minus deposited downtime windows, station coordinates, elevation, slope, aspect, habitat and six vegetation-cover classes.
reference: Bison, M., Yoccoz, N. G., Carlson, B. Z., Bayle, A., & Delestrade, A. (2024). Camera traps reveal seasonal variation in activity and occupancy of the Alpine mountain hare Lepus timidus varronis. Wildlife Biology, 2024(4), e01186.
notes: Record-table source (contact days) plus a camera table with setup dates and downtime windows but no end dates: survey set inferred to 2022-06-30 (abstract). Season binning is the processor's; the paper's occasion and season definitions were not reachable. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Weekly counts of independent grey wolf and brown bear camera-trap detections at 229 deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, up to 104 seven-day occasions per deployment, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: Matrices have no row ids; aligned to the covariate sheet by row order (229 each). 13 deployments have no surveyed week. Lynx counts not alignable (215 x 472); lynx 0/1 in blount_2025_neturkiye_lynx_occ.

description: Eurasian lynx detection / non-detection per seven-day occasion at 229 camera deployments (2009-2023) in and around Sarikamis-Allahuekber Mountains National Park, northeastern Turkiye, with camera, topographic, land-cover, distance and human-activity covariates; sibling of the wolf and bear count table.
reference: Blount, J. D., Green, A. M., Chynoweth, M., Coban, E., Kusak, J. & Sekercioglu, C. H. (2025). Combining N-mixture and occupancy analysis offers a more complete picture of carnivore habitat use in Northeastern Turkiye. PLOS One 20(5), e0320768.
notes: 0/1 only: the lynx count matrix (215 x 472, no ids) cannot be aligned to the deployments. Same survey set as blount_2025_neturkiye_carniv_count.

description: Camera-trap detection / non-detection of fishers at 64 sites x 64 sampling occasions, Alberta, 2016; the unmarked data set paired with the genetic SCR table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_scr.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Single-species camera detections, complete 64 x 64 matrix. No coordinates (site numbering not keyed to the TDF). Occasion length only in the paywalled-to-agents paper.

description: Genetic spatial capture-recapture detections of 24 fishers at 64 hair-snag sites over 4 occasions in Alberta, 2016 (one row per fisher x site x occasion), with UTM site coordinates in __traps.
reference: Burgar, J. M., Stewart, F. E. C., Volpe, J. P., Fisher, J. T., & Burton, A. C. (2018). Estimating density for species conservation: Comparing camera trap spatial count models to genetic spatial capture-recapture models. Global Ecology and Conservation, 15, e00411.
notes: Closed-population genetic SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = TDF usage (all sites, all occasions). Sibling camera table burgar_2018_alberta_fisher_count not joinable (different site numbering). Below floor (24 individuals).

description: Multi-state closed robust design capture histories of 209 photo-identified Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops aduncus) at three sites in Perth metropolitan waters, Western Australia: 16 seasonal primary periods (June 2011 to May 2015) x 3-6 secondary occasions; y is the site of capture (0 not captured, 1 estuary, 2 embayment, 3 open coast). The Program MARK input for Chabanne et al. (2017) Scenario 1.
reference: Chabanne, D.B.H., Pollock, K.H., Finn, H., Bejder, L. & Gimenez, O. (2017). Applying the multistate capture-recapture robust design to characterize metapopulation structure. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 8(11), 1547-1557.
notes: Season layout of the 75 unlabelled MARK columns inferred against the thesis effort table (76 completed occasions); summer 2011-12 carries 4 columns. 2-state (Scenario 2) file not shipped. One duplicated id relabelled.

description: Alder flycatcher removal counts (individuals first detected in each of three 5-minute intervals) at 50 points in Massachusetts beaver meadows, 2005, survey 1, with woody vegetation, structure, time and date covariates (unmarked alfl.csv; Chandler, King & DeStefano 2009). First multinomial_cell table.
reference: Chandler, R. B., King, D. I. & DeStefano, S. (2009). Scrub-shrub bird habitat associations at multiple spatial scales in beaver meadows in Massachusetts. The Auk 126(1), 186-197.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package. occasion indexes the removal interval (standard E9 declared stretch); multinomialType = removal. Round-trip tested in converters/rt_03_alfl_removal.R.

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with record counts in y_raw) of 35 bird and mammal taxa at 129 game cameras deployed about a week each at wildlife openings in the Monongahela National Forest, West Virginia, in April-May 2019, 2020 and 2021, with camera-hours per day as effort; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.
reference: Clipp, H. L., Pesi, S. M., Miller, M. L., Gigliotti, L. C., Skelly, B. P., & Rota, C. T. (2024). White-tailed deer detection rates increase when coyotes are present. Ecology and Evolution, 14(3), e11149.
notes: Wildlife-openings dataset only. The deposit also re-uploads Snapshot USA 2020 (third-party, not hosted) and a Wildlife Insights export licensed CC BY-NC (shipped separately as clipp_2024_wvprivate_comm).

description: Daily detection/non-detection (with sequence counts in y_raw) of 47 bird and mammal taxa at 146 game cameras deployed about two months each on private land in three West Virginia county pairs in summer 2022, with camera-hours per day as effort, coordinates and detection distance; one of three datasets behind a deer-coyote two-species occupancy paper.
reference: Clipp, H. L., Pesi, S. M., Miller, M. L., Gigliotti, L. C., Skelly, B. P., & Rota, C. T. (2024). White-tailed deer detection rates increase when coyotes are present. Ecology and Evolution, 14(3), e11149.
original_license: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record) / CC BY-NC (licence column of sequences.csv)
notes: Wildlife Insights export; the per-row CC BY-NC governs over the record's CC BY. Eight deployments beyond the paper's 138 shipped and marked in __units. Coordinates on private land as published; unit ids pseudonymised (deposited names are landowner surnames).

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array). Below floor (6 individuals). One script writes six species tables.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of genet (large-spotted genet complex) (Genetta) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array). Genus-rank taxon; mostly single-flank ids. One script writes six species tables.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of spotted hyaena (Crocuta crocuta) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array).  One script writes six species tables.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of leopard (Panthera pardus) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array).  One script writes six species tables.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of lion (Panthera leo) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array).  One script writes six species tables.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of serval (Leptailurus serval) at 100 camera sites in the Munywana Conservancy, South Africa, 17 Sept 2021 to 11 Jan 2022, individual x camera x day on the deposited operation matrix; trap coordinates centred on the array (local metres). One of six sibling tables from a multi-species design-optimisation study.
reference: Curveira-Santos, G., Dupont, G., Sutherland, C., Pretorius, C., Naylor, S., Allan, K., & Gigliotti, L. C. (2026). Optimizing camera-trap survey designs for multi-species density estimation using spatial capture-recapture models. Journal of Applied Ecology, 63(1).
notes: SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps in processor-centred local metres (VU taxa on the array).  One script writes six species tables.

description: Counts of 14 riparian landbird species on 4,712 five-minute 50 m point counts at 183 stations on 13 riparian transects in protected areas of Marin County, California (1997-2019; normally two visits per breeding season), with explicit zeros as deposited by Point Blue Conservation Science.
reference: Dettling, M.D., Dybala, K.E., Humple, D.L. & Gardali, T. (2021). Protected areas safeguard landbird populations in central coastal California: Evidence from long-term population trends. Ornithological Applications 123(4): duab035.
notes: Deposit is a per-survey species table with explicit zeros (14 of the species counted). No dates, observers or coordinates deposited. README species/row counts (17 / 80,104) differ from the file (14 / 65,968).

description: Spatial capture-recapture detections of 29 identified jaguars at 20 camera stations over 183 days in Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary, Belize (Aug 2013 - Feb 2014), one row per jaguar x station x operating day, with the time of each photograph and station coordinates (UTM 16N) in __traps.
reference: Distiller, G. B., Borchers, D. L., Foster, R. J., & Harmsen, B. J. (2020). Using Continuous-Time Spatial Capture-Recapture models to make inference about animal activity patterns. Ecology and Evolution, 10(20), 11826-11837.
notes: Closed-population SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps. Survey set = deposited station x day operating matrix. Detection times kept in obs_capture_time for the continuous-time model. Unsexed individuals included with unit_sex = U.

description: Detection/non-detection of 12 foliage-gleaning bird species on up to 3 replicate 10-minute point counts per year at 373 Hubbard Brook plots, 2010-2018, with elevation, coordinates (UTM 19N and WGS84), survey day and time (spOccupancy::hbefTrends; Doser et al. 2022 integrated community occupancy data). The package's hbef2015 is the 2015 slice.
reference: Doser, J. W., Leuenberger, W., Sillett, T. S., Hallworth, M. T. & Zipkin, E. F. (2022). Integrated community occupancy models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13, 919-932. Package: Doser, Finley, Kery & Zipkin (2022) MEE 13, 1670-1678.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package (spOccupancy); the underlying EDI deposit (edi.348) is behind an access wall for the builder. 45 covariate-only cells not surveyed. hbef2015 not shipped separately (identical 2015 slice).

description: Time-removal detections of 12 foliage-gleaning bird species (first-detection interval of three 2-minute intervals) at 80 NEON point-count sites in Bartlett Experimental Forest, NH, June 2015, with elevation, coordinates, survey day and hour (spOccupancy::neon2015; Doser et al. 2022). Two species never detected.
reference: Doser, J. W., Leuenberger, W., Sillett, T. S., Hallworth, M. T. & Zipkin, E. F. (2022). Integrated community occupancy models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13, 919-932. Package: Doser, Finley, Kery & Zipkin (2022) MEE 13, 1670-1678.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package (spOccupancy). Removal design on species detection (not individuals): occasion = 2-minute interval, multinomialType = removal; NA-after-detection in the package array shipped as 0.

description: American marten camera-trap detection/non-detection at 197 stations in Maine over seven summer/winter seasons of 33 occasions each (station activity varies by season: 197 active in S1, 26 in S4); no covariates or coordinates deposited.
reference: Evans, B. (2021). Marten detection history [Data set]. figshare.
notes: Occasion length and calendar years not stated in the deposit; seasons labelled S1-S4 / W1-W3 in __periods. No associated paper DOI on the deposit.

description: Camera-trap community data for 18 mammal species at 138 stations in cattle-grazed temperate forest along the China-Russia border, Northeast China: per station x species the number of 14-day windows with a detection and the number of windows surveyed (binomial_count), with 12 site covariates as deposited; no coordinates.
reference: Feng, J.-W., Sun, Y.-F., Li, H., Xiao, Y., Zhang, D., Smith, J. L. D., Ge, J., & Wang, T.-M. (2021). Assessing mammal species richness and occupancy in a Northeast Asian temperate forest shared by cattle. Diversity and Distributions, 27(5), 857-872.
notes: First binomial_count table (ruling #34): occasions collapsed by the authors to 14-day windows with a detection out of k surveyed. Held in batch 7, built in batch 10. Study year only in the paper (not fetchable).

description: Black-and-white Warbler point counts at 272 sites in Macon County, North Carolina (2010 or 2011), three visits each, with every visit coded 0 not detected / 1 unconfirmed detection / 2 confirmed detection; site coordinates, percent forest within 200 m and survey year as covariates. The false-positive occupancy example of Ferguson et al. (2015).
reference: Ferguson, P.F.B., Conroy, M.J., & Hepinstall-Cymerman, J. (2015). Occupancy models for data with false positive and false negative errors and heterogeneity across sites and surveys. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6(12), 1395-1406.
notes: Multi-state response (0/1/2 = none / uncertain / certain detection) for false-positive occupancy models (occuFP type 2). README labels the coordinates UTM but they are decimal degrees. Count protocol details are only in the paper.

description: Detection/non-detection of 74 fish species in 100 HUC12 watersheds of the Upper and Middle New River basin (Virginia/North Carolina) across 26 three-year primary periods (1938-2014), compiled from collection records; years within a period are secondary occasions and the number of collections per HUC-year is the effort covariate.
reference: Frimpong, E. (2017). Fish Detection Histories and Covariates, Upper and Middle New River Drainage Basin (Virginia and North Carolina, USA). Harvard Dataverse, V1.
notes: No associated paper identified on Crossref. Surveyed = at least one collection record that HUC-year.

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of guigna, Molina's hog-nosed skunk, foxes (Lycalopex), domestic dog and domestic cat at 180 grid-cell camera stations over up to 14 five-night occasions in agricultural landscapes of La Araucania, Chile (2019), with camera nights and human detections per occasion and 13 landscape metrics per station.
reference: Galvez, N., Infante, J., Fernandez, A., Diaz, J., & Petracca, L. (2021). Land use intensification coupled with free-roaming dogs as potential defaunation drivers of mesocarnivores in agricultural landscapes. Journal of Applied Ecology, 58(12), 2962-2974.
notes: Licence conflict: Dryad metadata CC0, deposited readme ODbL/DbCL; the stricter (ODbL) governs and propagates (intake policy). 693 of 2,520 unit-occasions not surveyed (trailing). Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Open-population spatial capture-recapture of tigers at Nagarahole Reserve, India (WCS, 1991-2000): 75 photo-identified individuals x 195 camera stations x 10 primary periods, y = trap days with a capture per station-period, effort = active trap days; station coordinates centred by the authors (local metres).
reference: Gardner, B., Sollmann, R., Kumar, N. S., Jathanna, D., & Karanth, K. U. (2018). State space and movement specification in open population spatial capture-recapture models. Ecology and Evolution, 8(20), 10336-10344.
notes: First open-population SCR table (E9 experimental). Station-period level (count + effort), no occasion: per-day effort not deposited. Coordinates centred by the source.

description: Calling index (0 none to 3 full chorus) of 14 frog and toad species inside the study plot on 2,216 night-time site visits at 70 Atchafalaya Basin sites, Louisiana (2008-2016), with the outside-plot index as a covariate, survey conditions, observers and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H., 2025, Data from time-constrained visual encounter surveys and acoustic surveys for amphibians and reptiles in the Atchafalaya Basin conducted from 2008 through 2016: U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Ordinal calling index (responseType ordinal, standard E2). Orphan Sample ID 348 and five 'done in error' samples dropped. Companion: glorioso_2025_atchafalaya_ves.

description: Counts of 47 amphibian and reptile species on 2,216 night-time time-constrained visual encounter surveys at 70 sites in the Atchafalaya Basin, Louisiana (2008-2016; 4-6 samples per site-year), with survey duration, weather and water variables, observers, and site coordinates.
reference: Glorioso, B.M., and Waddle, J.H., 2025, Data from time-constrained visual encounter surveys and acoustic surveys for amphibians and reptiles in the Atchafalaya Basin conducted from 2008 through 2016: U.S. Geological Survey data release.
notes: Zeros built from the sample table (a sample exists iff a row in Sample_Data). Orphan Sample ID 348 and five 'done in error' samples dropped. Companion table: glorioso_2025_atchafalaya_calls.

description: Central Greater Glider spotlight detection/non-detection at 34 road transects in Richmond Range National Park, NSW, three surveys per year for eight years (2014-2021; 20 to 34 transects over time), with seven deposited habitat covariates; multi-season occupancy design spanning the 2019 drought.
reference: Goldingay, R. L., McHugh, D. & Parkyn, J. L. (2022). Multiyear monitoring of threatened iconic arboreal mammals in a mid-elevation conservation reserve in eastern Australia. Ecology and Evolution 12(5): e8935.
notes: One of two tables from the deposit (companion: the koala); the species' survey sets differ in 22 cells so they are not one community table. No coordinates deposited. 2021 acoustic-recorder data not shipped.

description: Koala spotlight detection/non-detection at 34 road transects in Richmond Range National Park, NSW, three surveys per year for eight years (2014-2021; 20 to 34 transects over time), with seven deposited habitat covariates; multi-season occupancy design spanning the 2019 drought.
reference: Goldingay, R. L., McHugh, D. & Parkyn, J. L. (2022). Multiyear monitoring of threatened iconic arboreal mammals in a mid-elevation conservation reserve in eastern Australia. Ecology and Evolution 12(5): e8935.
notes: One of two tables from the deposit (companion: the greater glider); the species' survey sets differ in 22 cells so they are not one community table. No coordinates deposited. 2021 acoustic-recorder data not shipped.

description: Detection/non-detection of nine amphibian species (eggs, larvae or adults) at 100 ponds in Hungary over three combined visual/dip-net/trap surveys in 2023, with eight per-survey covariates (date, VES effort, water temperature and level, wind, rain, fish, emergent vegetation).
reference: Hamer, A. J., & Horanyi, J. (2024). Improving inference within freshwater community studies: Accounting for variable detection rates of amphibians and fish. Ecology and Evolution, 14(10), e70383.
notes: Fetched as the Dryad version zip (per-file API downloads need a bearer token). One pond-survey (T9, survey 1) not conducted.

description: Line-transect distance sampling counts of the federally endangered Mitchell's satyr butterfly (Neonympha mitchellii mitchellii) in five 1 m perpendicular-distance bins on 125 transect walks over five days in July 2011 at one site in lower Michigan, with transect length, management unit, temperature and humidity. First distance-sampling (multinomial_cell, distanceBreaks) table.
reference: Hamm, C. A. (2013). Estimating abundance of the federally endangered Mitchell's satyr butterfly using hierarchical distance sampling. Insect Conservation and Diversity, 6(5), 619-626.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = distance bin, distanceBreaks in metadata. Transects not matched across days; unit = date_transect. Endangered taxon, no coordinates in the deposit.

description: Detection/non-detection of 63 bird species on 1,055 point counts in 61 Karoo pentads, South Africa, 2017, with the time to first detection, distance and detection mode of each species on each count as observation covariates; count weather and location.
reference: Henry, D. A. W., Lee, A. T. K., & Altwegg, R. (2020). Can time-to-detection models with fewer survey replicates provide a robust alternative to traditional site-occupancy models? Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 11(5), 643-655.
notes: Record table of first detections; survey set = counts with at least one detection (row_presence). Time to detection carried as obs_ttd_s, not y (design_landscape C).

description: Thomson's gazelle detection/non-detection at 194 Snapshot Serengeti cameras over 46 consecutive 8-day windows (5,669 camera-windows with >= 1 operating day), with camera-days of effort, MODIS NDVI and a rainfall indicator per window, fire, tree-density classes, distance to river and camera coordinates.
reference: Hepler, S. A., Erhardt, R. J., Anderson, T. M. (2018). Identifying drivers of spatial variation in occupancy with limited replication camera trap data. Ecology 99(10):2152-2158.
notes: Rows exist only for camera-windows with >= 1 operating day (effort in obs_camera_days). Window start dates and the year are not deposited, so no date column. Coordinates as published (Least Concern taxon).

description: Disease-structured robust-design capture histories of 116 juvenile Fleay's barred frogs (Mixophyes fleayi, IUCN EN) at Brindle Creek, NSW: 8 primary periods x 2 weekly secondary surveys (14 surveyed), y = 0 not captured / 1 captured Bd-negative / 2 captured Bd-positive from up to four qPCR runs per swab, with runs, positives and mean ITS copies per capture.
reference: Hollanders, M. & Royle, J.A. (2022). Know what you don't know: Embracing state uncertainty in disease-structured multistate models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 13(12), 2827-2837.
notes: qPCR runs (the authors' multievent fourth level) summarised per capture; two skipped surveys are missing rows; no dates, coordinates or covariates deposited.

description: Tiger sign-survey occupancy across India: 7,183 100 km2 grid cells x four estimation cycles (2006-2018), each cell-cycle as replicates with tiger sign out of replicates surveyed (binomial_count), with eight static and five cycle-varying standardised covariates; no coordinates.
reference: Jhala, Y. V., Mungi, N. A., Gopal, R., & Qureshi, Q. (2025). Tiger recovery amid people and poverty. Science, 387(6733), 505-510.
notes: binomial_count (ruling #34): replicate-level histories not deposited. Covariates standardised by the authors. dpat (distance to tiger-occupied PA, derived from the previous cycle's survey) not shipped. Science paper paywalled; protocol from the sheet dictionary.

description: Mallard counts on up to 3 surveys of 239 Swiss MHB 1-km2 quadrats (235 surveyed), with standardised elevation, transect length, forest, survey intensity and date (unmarked::mallard; Kery, Royle & Schmid 2005).
reference: Kery, M., Royle, J. A. & Schmid, H. (2005). Modeling avian abundance from replicated counts using binomial mixture models. Ecological Applications 15(4), 1450-1461.

description: Willow tit detection/non-detection on 3 surveys of 237 Swiss MHB 1-km2 quadrats, with standardised elevation, forest, transect length, survey date and intensity (unmarked widewt.csv; the dataset of the unmarked overview vignette and AHM1 ch. 10).
reference: Fiske, I. & Chandler, R. (2011). unmarked: An R package for fitting hierarchical models of wildlife occurrence and abundance. Journal of Statistical Software 43(10).
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package; covariates standardised in the source. Round-trip tested in converters/rt_01_willowtit_occu.R.

description: European crossbill detection/non-detection on up to 3 surveys per year, 1999-2007, at 267 Swiss MHB 1-km2 quadrats, with elevation, forest cover and survey date (unmarked::crossbill; the colext vignette and AHM2 ch. 4 dataset).
reference: Fiske, I. & Chandler, R. (2011). unmarked: An R package for fitting hierarchical models of wildlife occurrence and abundance. Journal of Statistical Software 43(10).

description: Counts of 158 bird species on up to 3 surveys of 267 Swiss MHB 1-km2 quadrats in 2014, with quadrat coordinates (unspecified CRS), elevation, route length, forest, survey date and duration, observer and species traits (AHMbook::MHB2014; the AHM1 ch. 11 community dataset).
reference: Kery, M. & Royle, J. A. (2016). Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology, vol. 1. Academic Press. Ch. 11.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package. Counts shipped (the book collapses to 0/1). 13 species never recorded ship as all-zero taxa. Round-trip tested (as 0/1) in converters/rt_06_mhb2014_community.R.

description: Cormack-Jolly-Seber capture histories of 313 wing-marked adult Calopteryx exul (Glittering Demoiselle, IUCN EN) over 25 daily sampling occasions on the Seybouse River, Guelma, Algeria, 2011, with sex and daily water depth.
reference: Khelifa, R., Mahdjoub, H., Baaloudj, A., Cannings, R. A., & Samways, M. J. (2021). Effects of both climate change and human water demand on a highly threatened damselfly. Scientific Reports, 11, 7725.
notes: Julian-day origin not stated; no calendar date derived. One site; coordinate given at 0.1 degree in geographicCoverage.

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of small rodents and small mustelids (two functional groups) at 48 cameras in 8 blocks on the Varanger Peninsula, Norway, over 7 seasons of 304 days (COAT programme, 2015-2020); the deposited four-state code is kept in y_raw.
reference: Kleiven, E. F. et al. Data and code to replicate "A dynamic occupancy model for interacting species with two spatial scales". DataverseNO.
notes: Taxa are functional groups (order / genus rank), not species. Calendar dates of the day index are not deposited. Two-spatial-scale design: cluster_id = block.

description: Northern shoveler counts on up to 10 visits to 50 wetlands in southern and east-central Sweden within one breeding season, with wetland water area, reed cover, RT90 northing and the Julian day of each visit (Knape et al. 2018, N-mixture overdispersion case study).
reference: Knape, J., Arlt, D., Barraquand, F., Berg, A., Chevalier, M., Part, T., Ruete, A. & Zmihorski, M. (2018). Sensitivity of binomial N-mixture models to overdispersion: the importance of assessing model fit. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 9(10), 2102-2114.
notes: Clean 50 x 10 count matrix with per-visit Julian days (no year deposited, so no ISO date) and three site covariates; 19 unsurveyed cells. Same data as nmixgof::shoveler.

description: Daily counts of independent moose detections at 72 camera traps over 91 winter days (Dec 2020-Mar 2021) in the John Prince Research Forest, British Columbia, under the 5-minute independence criterion, with the 30-minute and 8-hour recodings alongside (Koetke et al. 2024, N-mixture model-selection study).
reference: Koetke, L. J., Hodder, D. P. & Johnson, C. J. (2024). Using camera traps and N-mixture models to estimate population abundance: model selection really matters. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 15(5), 900-915.
notes: 72 cameras x 91 days, 617 inactive camera-days as missing rows; three independence criteria deposited, 5-min as y; no coordinates or covariates; aerial survey sheet not shipped.

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of 46 taxa (45 mammals incl. tiger, Asian elephant, dhole, clouded leopard, pangolin, plus the Bengal monitor) at 518 camera stations in six protected areas across Myanmar over up to 17 ten-day occasions (2014-2020), with camera days per occasion and six environmental predictors at five buffer scales per station.
reference: Kyaw, P. P., Cushman, S. A., Kaszta, Z., Burnham, D., Zaw, T., Naing, H., ... Macdonald, D. W. (2024). Seeing the big- to fine-grained picture: exploring the baseline status of mammal occupancy across Myanmar using scale-optimised modelling. Diversity and Distributions, 30(11), e13934.
notes: Built from the authors' pooled national matrices (Myan_o10, Myan_Effort, MyanCovs); survey membership from the per-survey effort files. 5,746 of 8,806 station-occasions not surveyed. No coordinates in the deposit. Moonrat (per-site only) not shipped. Deposited as a .rar; fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of Long-tailed mouse (Pseudomys higginsi) in four 60-trap Elliott grids in southern Tasmanian forests over six 5-night sessions (March and May 2009-2011), individual x trap x night, with trap coordinates (UTM 55S). Companion table for the other small mammal; devil and cat camera captures in the deposit not shipped.
reference: Lazenby, B. T., Mooney, N. J., & Dickman, C. R. (2021). Raiders of the last ark: the impacts of feral cats on small mammals in Tasmanian forest ecosystems. Ecological Applications, 31(6), e02362.
notes: First SCR table (E9 experimental). Trap usage inferred (all 60 traps x 5 nights every session). One script writes two tables (one per species); camera-trap predators held.

description: Spatial capture-recapture histories of Swamp rat (Rattus lutreolus) in four 60-trap Elliott grids in southern Tasmanian forests over six 5-night sessions (March and May 2009-2011), individual x trap x night, with trap coordinates (UTM 55S). Companion table for the other small mammal; devil and cat camera captures in the deposit not shipped.
reference: Lazenby, B. T., Mooney, N. J., & Dickman, C. R. (2021). Raiders of the last ark: the impacts of feral cats on small mammals in Tasmanian forest ecosystems. Ecological Applications, 31(6), e02362.
notes: First SCR table (E9 experimental). Trap usage inferred (all 60 traps x 5 nights every session). One script writes two tables (one per species); camera-trap predators held.

description: Detection/non-detection of 34 boreal songbird species within 150 m of autonomous recording units at 564 locations (three positions across each of 189 regenerating harvest edges in Alberta), 1-5 visits per location in one season; position, forest type, years since harvest, spruce cover on each side, coordinates, standardised visit day and time.
reference: Lebeuf-Taylor, I., Lebeuf-Taylor, E., & Bayne, E. (in prep). Contrast between adjoining stands drives timber harvest edge effects on boreal birds. Data: Borealis, doi:10.5683/SP4/FH7WY6.
notes: Analysis-ready Stan input (.rds); survey year, dates and recording length not deposited; visit day and time only as z-scores. Paper in prep (no DOI, 2026-11-01).

description: Capture histories of 294 European dippers over 7 annual occasions (1981-1987) in eastern France, with sex (marked::dipper; Lebreton et al. 1992). The standard CJS textbook example.
reference: Lebreton, J.-D., Burnham, K. P., Clobert, J. & Anderson, D. R. (1992). Modeling survival and testing biological hypotheses using marked animals. Ecological Monographs 62(1), 67-118.
notes: Textbook dataset bundled with an R package. Round-trip tested in converters/rt_04_dipper_cjs.R.

description: Route totals of 270 bird taxa on 11,011 annual counts of 1,256 Swedish Bird Survey summer point count routes (20 points x 5 minutes, free-choice routes, 1975-2024), with date, start/end time, observer id, transport, county and 25 km grid-square centre; built from the GBIF Darwin Core event core (survey set) and per-species occurrence records.
reference: Lindström Å, Green M, Jönsson A (2025). Swedish Bird Survey: Summer point count routes (Sommarpunktrutterna). Version 1.8. Department of Biology, Lund University. Sampling event dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/2aajk9 accessed via GBIF.org.
notes: Survey set = DwC event core (every route count; protocol registers all species; noObservations false everywhere). One count per route per year, 20 points summed by the source, so no within-year replication. Eleven security-class-4 raptors/owls/storks withheld by the publisher (no rows). Coordinates are 25 x 25 km grid centres as published. Fetched as the IPT Darwin Core Archive.

description: Camera-trap detection/non-detection of chilla fox, culpeo fox, guigna and domestic dog at 48 camera stations over up to 12 seven-day occasions in a fragmented agricultural landscape of Los Lagos, Chile (2019), with six camera-level habitat covariates.
reference: Malhotra, R., Jimenez, J., & Harris, N. (2021). Patch characteristics and domestic dogs differentially affect carnivore space use in fragmented landscapes in southern Chile. Diversity and Distributions, 27(12).
notes: Files fetched from the Zenodo mirror (record 5106824) because anonymous Dryad downloads return 401. Dog_occu (model output) not shipped.

description: Counts of 112 bird species on breeding-season point counts at 260 points along forest rights-of-way and controls in the central Appalachians (2016-2019), two visits per point per treatment-relative year (pre, +1, +2), with date, observer, time and treatment code; built from per-individual detection records, flyovers excluded.
reference: Margenau, E. L., Wood, P. B., & Rota, C. T. (2022). Habitat management for stopover and breeding songbird communities along rights-of-way in forest-dominated landscapes. Ecological Applications, 32(3), e2540.
notes: Zeros inferred: a point-year-visit is a survey iff it has at least one detection row (four explicit Count = 0 rows show empty counts were logged). Flyovers (75 rows) excluded; UNCH/UNWO/BARO dropped; CAGO merged into CANG. Stopover file not converted. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Weekly camera-trap detection/non-detection (with the number of detection episodes in y_raw) of 18 mammal species at 355 game cameras across an urban-to-rural gradient in Northwest Arkansas over two winter seasons (16 and 22 weeks), with camera-days per week as effort and study site as cluster.
reference: McTigue, L. E., & DeGregorio, B. A. (2024). Nine-banded Armadillo (Dasypus novemcinctus) occupancy and density across an urban-to-rural gradient. Southeastern Naturalist, 23(4), 529-548.
notes: Built from a per-detection record table: surveyed camera-weeks inferred from first/last detection per camera-year (deployment dates in the file are inconsistent). Density/covariate file unjoinable (site labels differ). Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Genetic (scat) spatial capture-recapture detections of 37 river otters at 20 latrines over 8 occasions, Upper Rio Grande, New Mexico, 2018 (one row per otter x surveyed latrine-occasion), with UTM latrine coordinates in __traps and the conservative individual id as a unit covariate.
reference: Murphy, S. M., Adams, J. R., Waits, L. P., & Cox, J. J. (2021). Evaluating otter reintroduction outcomes using genetic spatial capture-recapture modified for dendritic networks. Ecology and Evolution, 11, 15047-15061.
notes: Closed-population genetic SCR (E9 experimental): trap key + __traps; the authors used a dendritic (network-distance) state space, not shipped. unit = lenient individual (37); unit_conservative_id collapses to the authors' preferred 30. One detection at an unlisted latrine not shipped.

description: Daily multi-state camera-trap observations of coyotes (0 none / 1 detected / 2 detected with visible sarcoptic mange signs) at 115 Chicago-area camera stations over 16 seasons (2010-2014, 28 days each), with per-day image-quality covariates, site urbanisation covariates and coordinates.
reference: Murray, M. H., Fidino, M., Lehrer, E. W., Simonis, J. L., & Magle, S. B. (2021). A multi-state occupancy model to non-invasively monitor visible signs of wildlife health with camera traps that accounts for image quality. Journal of Animal Ecology, 90(8), 1973-1985.
notes: Multi-state (disease) occupancy. Survey set from the deposited daily operability flag (NA = inactive). 285 images outside windows / on inactive days dropped as in the authors' code. UTM 16N converted to WGS84. Fetched as the Dryad version zip.

description: Number of carabid beetle individuals of 55 species per pitfall-trap sample (~14-day bouts, biweekly through the growing season) at 2029 traps on 47 NEON terrestrial sites, 2013-2023, built from NEON's sorting records (RELEASE-2026) with trapping days, trap condition and plot-centre coordinates as published.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Ground beetles sampled from pitfall traps (DP1.10022.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/q9ne-6b77
notes: Token-gated NEON API (NEON_TOKEN); release pinned. National species pool (>= 1000 individuals); sorting-level ids; bycatch and morphospecies not shipped.

description: Number of individuals of 283 bird species per 6-minute point count at 3434 points on 47 NEON terrestrial sites, 2013-2024 (one or two bouts per breeding season), built from NEON's per-detection records (RELEASE-2026) with observer, date-time, weather and habitat per count and point coordinates as published.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Breeding landbird point counts (DP1.10003.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/v6hs-mx57
notes: Token-gated NEON API (NEON_TOKEN); release pinned. National species pool (>= 100 clusters); fuzzed higher-rank IDs and minute-88 detections not shipped. Sibling: neon_2026_landbirds_ds.

description: Clusters of 46 common bird species in four radial-distance bins (0-25, 25-50, 50-100, 100-1000 m) per 6-minute point count at 3434 points on 47 NEON terrestrial sites, 2013-2024, with individuals per bin, observer, date-time, weather and habitat; built from NEON's per-detection distances (RELEASE-2026). Sibling of neon_2026_landbirds_count.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Breeding landbird point counts (DP1.10003.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/v6hs-mx57
notes: Continuous distances binned by the processor (4 bins); species with >= 2000 clusters only; period = count event. Token-gated NEON API; release pinned.

description: Robust-design capture histories of 3,435 ear- or PIT-tagged Microtus pennsylvanicus on 64 NEON Sherman-trap grids at 16 sites across the United States, 2014-2024: one row per individual x surveyed night of its home grid from first capture on (bout = period, night = occasion), y = captured, with sex, weight, life stage, traps set and grid method. One of 4 species tables from the same deposit.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34
notes: Conditional on first capture; rows to the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release. One script writes 4 species tables (ruling #20). Sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_count (grid counts, coordinates).

description: Robust-design capture histories of 13,647 ear- or PIT-tagged Peromyscus leucopus on 146 NEON Sherman-trap grids at 25 sites across the United States, 2013-2024: one row per individual x surveyed night of its home grid from first capture on (bout = period, night = occasion), y = captured, with sex, weight, life stage, traps set and grid method. One of 4 species tables from the same deposit.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34
notes: Conditional on first capture; rows to the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release. One script writes 4 species tables (ruling #20). Sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_count (grid counts, coordinates).

description: Robust-design capture histories of 17,503 ear- or PIT-tagged Peromyscus maniculatus on 211 NEON Sherman-trap grids at 32 sites across the United States, 2013-2024: one row per individual x surveyed night of its home grid from first capture on (bout = period, night = occasion), y = captured, with sex, weight, life stage, traps set and grid method. One of 4 species tables from the same deposit.

notes: Conditional on first capture; rows to the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release. One script writes 4 species tables (ruling #20). Sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_count (grid counts, coordinates).

description: Robust-design capture histories of 4,474 ear- or PIT-tagged Sigmodon hispidus on 72 NEON Sherman-trap grids at 13 sites across the United States, 2013-2024: one row per individual x surveyed night of its home grid from first capture on (bout = period, night = occasion), y = captured, with sex, weight, life stage, traps set and grid method. One of 4 species tables from the same deposit.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34
notes: Conditional on first capture; rows to the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release. One script writes 4 species tables (ruling #20). Sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_count (grid counts, coordinates).

description: Nightly capture counts of 143 small mammal species on 332 NEON Sherman-trap grids (10 x 10, 10 m) at 46 sites across the United States, 2013-2024, in 1612 bouts of 1-3 nights (robust-design counts: bout = period, night = occasion), with traps set per night as effort and NEON plot coordinates as published; national species pool, sites per species in __taxa.
reference: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34
notes: First NEON table; built through the token-gated NEON API (download_neon in lib). National species pool (E4 rectangle); taxon_sites in __taxa. Captures above species rank (genus, species group) not shipped. Sibling: neon_2026_smallmammals_rd.

description: Counts of 50 bird species on 150 ten-minute, 100 m point counts (50 points x 3 surveys, 12 May-2 June 2011) in four habitat types on six islands of the Yalalii (Goose Island) Archipelago, British Columbia, built from the deposited per-detection records under the authors' own counting rule; start time, temperature, weather, observer and point coordinates.
reference: Obrist, D.S., Pendray, J.E., Field, R.D., Housty, W.G., Reynolds, J.D. et al. (2024). Comparing historical and contemporary observations of avian fauna on the Yalalii (Goose Island) Archipelago, British Columbia, Canada. Ecology and Evolution 14(12): e70464.
notes: Per-detection deposit; y = detections in minutes 1-10 within 100 m (reproduces the authors' summary sheet). Detections outside that rule not shipped. Coordinates as published (no flagged taxa).

description: Robust-design tag-resight histories of 1,729 female southern elephant seals (Mirounga leonina) at Marion Island over 28 seal years (breeding seasons 1986-2013), three capture periods per year (uneven breeding weeks, even breeding weeks, moult and winter); y = seen, y_raw = the authors' 8-level composite event code used in their multievent-robust design model.
reference: Oosthuizen, W. C., Pradel, R., Bester, M. N., & de Bruyn, P. J. N. (2019). Making use of multiple surveys: Estimating breeding probability using a multievent-robust design capture-recapture model. Ecology and Evolution, 9, 836-848.
notes: First robust-design table. Composite event codes decomposed losslessly into three capture-period rows per seal year; the event code is y_raw. Histories condition on first breeding encounter; leading zeros kept.

description: Presence/absence of 43 bird species at 10 point-count stations in east-central Argentina over 4 seasons x 5 visits (200 surveys per point), with 19 species-level functional traits (body mass, diet, foraging stratum, foraging behaviour) in the taxa side table.
reference: Palacio, F. X., Maragliano, R. E., & Montalti, D. (2020). The costs of ignoring species detectability on functional diversity estimation. The Auk, 137(4), ukaa057.
notes: Files fetched from the Zenodo mirror (record 4728255). 10 sites: below the proposed 30-unit floor, but 43 species x 20 surveys per site.

description: Line-transect distance sampling counts of 115 bird taxa in seven perpendicular-distance bands (0-100 m) on 19 surveys of eight 1,200 m transects across habitat strata in Mudumalai and the Upper Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu, India, 1995-96, with survey duration and weather; transect coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree.
reference: Raman, T. R. S. (2001). Community ecology and conservation of mid-elevation tropical rainforest bird communities in the southern Western Ghats, India. PhD thesis, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = distance band, distanceBreaks in metadata; period = visit index (1-4 visits per transect). 5 of 1,491 detections dropped (beyond 100 m, ambiguous or missing band). 'sp.' records at genus rank.

description: Camera-trap community survey of 44 mammal species at 221 stations in northern Botswana (Rich et al. 2016): nights with a detection out of nights surveyed per station x species (binomial counts, 6,607 trap nights), six station covariates, diet and body-size traits per species; coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree (EN/VU taxa present).
reference: Rich, L. N., Miller, D. A. W., Robinson, H. S., McNutt, J. W., & Kelly, M. J. (2016). Using camera trapping and hierarchical occupancy modelling to evaluate the spatial ecology of an African mammal community. Journal of Applied Ecology, 53(4), 1225-1235.
notes: First binomial_count table (ruling #34): night-level histories not deposited, y = nights detected out of obs_trials. Traits (diet, body size class) in __taxa. Exact station coordinates in the deposit coarsened to 0.1 degree (wild dog, elephant EN; cheetah, lion, leopard, giraffe, hippo VU).

description: Robust-design capture histories of 7,845 female black brant (Branta bernicla nigricans) at the Tutakoke River colony, Alaska, 27 breeding seasons (1988-2014) x 3 capture methods (nest searches, tower resighting, banding drives); y = detected; banding year and age class, and gosling tarsus length for 713 females, as covariates.
reference: Riecke, T. V., Leach, A. G., Gibson, D., & Sedinger, J. S. (2018). Parameterizing the robust design in the BUGS language: Lifetime carry-over effects of environmental conditions during growth on a long-lived bird. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(11), 2294-2305.
notes: Built from the deposited R workspace (obs array). Occasions are capture methods within a season. Leading zeros before first detection kept; the paper conditions on first detection.

description: Weekly camera-trap detection/non-detection (sequence counts in y_raw) of 87 mammal species at 9,694 Snapshot USA deployments in 263 arrays across the United States, autumn 2019-2023, with camera-days per week as effort, array as cluster_id, habitat and development class, and 0.1-degree coarsened coordinates.
reference: Shamon, H., Maor, R., Cove, M. V., Kays, R., et al. (2024). SNAPSHOT USA 2021: A third coordinated national camera trap survey of the United States. Ecology, 105(6), e4318; Cove et al. (2021) Ecology 102:e03353; Kays et al. (2022) Ecology 103:e3775.
notes: Built from Dryad version 3 (2025-01-03; version 6 needs a token). 87 of 130 mammal species (>= 50 sequences); birds and higher-rank labels not shipped. Coordinates coarsened (red wolf CR, giant kangaroo rat EN among the taxa).

description: Dependent double-observer helicopter counts of waterfowl flocks (15 duck and goose species) on 27 plots in Labrador, Canada, June 2009: flocks detected by the primary observer pair and flocks missed by them but detected by the secondary pair, with plot area, observer position and experience. First double-observer (multinomial_cell) table.
reference: Roy, C., Gilliland, S. G., & Reed, E. T. (2022). A hierarchical dependent double-observer method for estimating waterfowl breeding pairs abundance from helicopters. Wildlife Biology, 2022(1), e01003.
notes: Declared stretch (E9): occasion = detection cell, multinomialType = dep_double_observer. 23 plots without the protocol and one plot with an unattributed flock not shipped (27 of 52 plots; below floor; the paper says 29 plots ran the protocol, the deposit attributes 28). Counts are flocks, not birds.

description: Daily camera-trap detection/non-detection of Baird's tapir at 22 cameras (6-72 camera-days each) in Rio Indio, Nicaragua, June-August 2014, with camera-days of effort and coarsened (0.1 degree) camera coordinates.
reference: Schank, C. (2015). Tapir detection histories (Tapirus bairdii) from Rio Indio, Nicaragua [Data set]. Zenodo.
notes: No associated paper identified. Coordinates coarsened to a 0.1-degree grid (Endangered taxon). 22 units: below the proposed 30-unit floor.

description: Sample-level eDNA detection (0/1, any of three qPCR replicates) of the Columbia spotted frog in three filter samples at each of 168 sites nested in 61 Great Basin watersheds (Oregon, Idaho, Nevada), 2015-2016, with site and watershed covariates; the authors' multi-scale occupancy input. First eDNA / multi-scale table.
reference: Smith, M. M., & Goldberg, C. S. (2020). Occupancy in dynamic systems: accounting for multiple scales and false positives using environmental DNA to inform monitoring. Ecography, 43(3), 376-386.
notes: Experimental (E9): cluster_id = watershed, unit = site, occasion = filter sample. No readme in the deposit; column meanings from the paper. Companion qPCR-level table from the same deposit cannot be joined to this one.

description: qPCR-replicate detections (0/1; 3 replicates x 3 filter samples) of Columbia spotted frog eDNA at 168 Great Basin sites, 2015-2016, with the site-level visual/dipnet confirmation as a covariate; the authors' false-positive occupancy input. Companion to smith_2019_greatbasin_csf_edna.
reference: Smith, M. M., & Goldberg, C. S. (2020). Occupancy in dynamic systems: accounting for multiple scales and false positives using environmental DNA to inform monitoring. Ecography, 43(3), 376-386.
notes: Experimental (E9): cluster_id = site, unit = filter sample, occasion = qPCR replicate. Visual/dipnet confirmation (occuFP code 2) recoded to a 0/1 site covariate. No watershed key in this file.

description: Counts of 105 bird species on 2,202 ten-minute 150 m point counts at 101 grid points across Powdermill Nature Reserve, Pennsylvania (2013-2025), two visits per point per breeding season, with date-time, observer, weather, point coordinates and elevation; built from the GBIF Darwin Core event core (survey set) and per-individual occurrence records.
reference: Sullivan K (2026). Powdermill Nature Reserve Bird Point Count Surveys. Version 1.3. Carnegie Museums. Sampling event dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/23qhtm accessed via GBIF.org.
notes: Survey set = DwC event core; Humboldt extension declares full Aves scope with abundance. Time bins and inner/outer circle exist only as remarks, so y is the 10-minute total. UNWO, two impossible species (STCA, LUWA), 40 empty 'Absent' placeholder rows and one unnamed point dropped; YSFL->NOFL, SCJU->DEJU. Fetched as the IPT Darwin Core Archive.

description: Annual capture histories of 707 adult female timber rattlesnakes (Crotalus horridus) at six dens in the southeastern Adirondacks, New York, over 26 sampling years 1983-2019 (unequal intervals), with den and colour morph per snake and two population-level annual covariates in __periods.
reference: Tetzlaff, S. J., Hileman, E. T., Simon, M. G., Schuett, G. W., Davis, M. A., & Brown, W. S. (2026). Population dynamics of a long-lived pitviper inferred from capture-recapture data spanning four decades. Ecosphere.
notes: First reptile capture-recapture table. MARK .inp with den x morph groups; nine snakes recorded at two dens kept as one unit with both dens listed. Unequal sampling intervals in __periods.
